arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. O'Connor argued the case involves the IRS authority to assess FICA taxes on tips.
Ms. Power argued Congress did not saddle employers with a tax while depriving them of a defense.
Ms. Power claimed the tax is not authorized because Congress did not require this action for thirty years.
Ms. O'Connor stated tips are deemed paid at a specific time under the statute.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Employers face financial liability for FICA taxes on tips. The outcome determines whether employers must pay these taxes without a prior legal defense. This affects how the IRS collects taxes from businesses.
